content.prompt: What's wrong with this stream? It compiles, but produces NO output.
content.hint: Streams are LAZY — nothing executes without a terminal operation
content.expectedOutput: Missing terminal operation (collect, forEach, count, etc.)

content.text: A stream is like a factory assembly line. Raw materials (data source) enter one end. Workers at stations along the belt transform or filter items (intermediate operations). At the END of the belt, a packer boxes the results (terminal operation). Key insight: NO worker does ANYTHING until the packer at the end starts requesting items. The line is lazy — it pulls items through on demand, not pushes them.

content.code:
List<Integer> prices = List.of(120, 45, 89, 200, 30, 150);

long count = prices.stream()
    .filter(p -> p > 50)             // keep prices > 50
    .map(p -> p * 0.9)               // apply 10% discount
    .filter(p -> p < 150)            // keep under 150
    .count();                        // terminal: count results
content.annotation: Stream pipeline = Source → Intermediate ops (lazy) → Terminal op (triggers execution). Intermediate: filter, map, sorted, distinct, limit, skip, flatMap — they return a new Stream and do nothing until triggered. Terminal: collect, forEach, count, reduce, findFirst, anyMatch — they trigger the pipeline and produce a final result. A stream can only be consumed ONCE — after a terminal operation, the stream is closed. Reusing throws IllegalStateException.

content.modification: What happens when you use a stream twice?
content.question: Can you call a terminal operation on the same stream object again?
content.explanation: A stream can ONLY be consumed once. After a terminal operation like forEach, the stream is closed. Attempting to reuse it throws IllegalStateException. Always create a new stream from the source if you need to process again — just like the factory assembly line can't rewind; you must feed new raw materials from the start.

content.label: collect() vs reduce() — building collections vs computing a single value
content.question: When do you use collect() vs reduce()?
options: collect for collections — reduce for single values
content.explanation: collect() is a terminal operation that builds a new collection (List, Set, Map). reduce() is a terminal operation that combines all elements into a single value (sum, max). Both trigger the pipeline, but collect produces a collection while reduce produces one result — like the packer at the end of the assembly line either boxes items into a crate (collect) or weighs the total (reduce).

content.question: Does peek() execute without a terminal operation?
content.explanation: ZERO output. Streams are lazy — without a terminal operation, NO intermediate operations execute. peek is intermediate, just like filter and map. The assembly line workers do nothing until the packer (terminal operation) at the end starts requesting items. Add .count() or .collect() to trigger the pipeline.
